handback.t:
TEAM B has reached the ~B50 target: rounds B40 to B50 are done and committed on branch teamB in C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh-teamB. Nothing was pushed and Team A's main was not touched. Lib suite is 385 pass (baseline was about 376). No retrieval or accuracy claim was made, so none of the retrieval iron rules were triggered.

Cherry-pick, in order:
- 2fa76b1 covers B40, B41 and B42.
- afb40f1 covers B43 to B50 and depends on 2fa76b1.
- Both touch src/store.rs, src/bin/meshstore.rs and RD-LOG-B.md (the log is updated through B50).

I did not pursue a memory-sharing or routing win, because I had no principled idea outside the rejected variants. The rounds went on tombstone hardening and sync correctness instead.

Bug fixes and features (all opt-in, defaults and old files unchanged):
- **B40, expiry and authority.**
  - `sync_docs_folder_with` takes `DocSyncOpts { propagate_deletions, tombstone_ttl_ms, deleters, now_ms }`.
  - Tombstone lines gain an optional origin timestamp `ts`. Lines without one never expire, and relays keep the origin timestamp.
  - Expired tombstones are ignored when read from peers, compacted out of the local files, and not exported. They are counted in `tombstones_expired`.
  - Only machines in `deleters` can delete. Other peers' deletions are counted in `deletions_unauthorized`.
  - Trade-off, stated and asserted in a test: after expiry, a peer that still holds the doc re-introduces it. The TTL must exceed the longest peer absence.
  - Authority is by machine id from the shard file name, so it guards against accidents and unvetted peers, not a malicious writer of the folder.
  - CLI: `meshstore sync-docs ... [--propagate-deletions] [--ttl-days N] [--deleters a,b]`.
  - The new tests call the new API, so on old code they fail to compile rather than at runtime.
- **B42, canonical gc.** `gc_docs_canonical` (CLI `gc-docs --canonical`) runs first-wins in doc-id order instead of row order, so machines converge on the same representatives. In the B41 fuzz (60 seeds, same ops and seeds), row-order gc left 46 of 60 seeds with different representatives per store. Canonical gc left 0 of 60. A mutation check confirms the fuzz can catch the keeper-rule failure.
- **B43, race fix.** The tombstone check in the sync import now happens under the store lock. A gc that tombstones an id between the sync's snapshot and its write can no longer be undone by that import. A deterministic test covers it.
- **B46.** `sync-docs` flag parsing returns a usage error with exit 2 instead of panicking.

Verified invariants and negatives (no code change):
- **B41, deletion-exchange fuzz.** Over 60 seeds, no duplicate class is ever lost and vector rows stay aligned. Disabling the keeper-present rule makes it fail.
- **B44, capped journal sync.** Every store converges to exactly the newest-K-per-world of the union, 60 of 60. No bug found.
- **B48, fuzz with tombstone expiry.** No class lost, and canonical gc still converges 60 of 60.
- **B45, B49.** B45 was a manual CLI end-to-end run of the new flags and is not automated. B49 updated the meshstore header docs.
- **B47, concurrent gc-versus-sync stress.** It passes, but it does not discriminate. With the B43 fix reverted it still passed in 3 of 3 runs, so only B43's deterministic test counts as proof.

Still open: a cryptographic identity for deleters.
